t071.sum: The confusion and trials of Urantia signify not God's indifference but part of the divine plan to forge strong and noble characters between the anvils of necessity and the hammers of anguish. Virtues such as courage, altruism, hope, and faith can grow only in a world of hardship and uncertainty. Jesus corrected the superstition that suffering is God's punishment, and while he did not exempt believers from difficulty, he promised to go with them through all their trials.
t071.s1.i1: The uncertainties and vicissitudes of life are in no way contradictory to the universal sovereignty of God.
t071.s1.i3: Altruism requires inequality, hope requires insecurity, and faith requires a situation in which one must believe more than one knows.
t071.s1.i4: Even the satisfaction of happiness is truly experienced only in a world open to the possibility of pain and distress.
t071.s1.i5: The perfect beings of Havona know neither the sweetness of escaping the potential of pain nor saving faith.
t071.s2.h: The Anvil and Hammer That Forge Character
t071.s2.i1: The Creators could make Urantia a paradise, but such an Eden would not produce strong and noble characters.
t071.s2.i5: God sometimes disciplines us for our good, but he suffers with us in our fiery trials.
t071.s3.i1: Jesus declared superstitious the belief that prosperity is a sign of God's approval and adversity a sign of his displeasure.
t071.s3.i2: Those killed by the falling tower of Siloam were not greater sinners but innocent victims of the accidents of time.
t071.s3.i3: As the story of Job shows, material prosperity is no proof of God's favor, and the Father loves the poor just as much.
t071.s3.i4: People suffer from the accidents of time, from imperfection, from the consequences of sin, and from the harvest of rebellion; suffering is not a visitation of divine judgment.
t071.s3.i5: Even in suffering Job pierced the clouds by faith and found the God of comfort and salvation.
t071.s4.i2: Believing the gospel does not exempt one from accidents and calamities, but it keeps one unafraid when trouble comes.
t071.s4.i4: In times of testing a person's soul is revealed, and the loyal who endure trials are entrusted with the work of the kingdom.
t071.s4.i5: Even when floods of adversity and hatred sweep over the soul, the one who entrusts his soul to the indwelling spirit has a citadel of the spirit that does not fall.
t071.s4.i6: True religion produces profound courage and confidence even in natural adversity and physical calamity.
t071.s5.i1: Jesus met suffering with faith, courage, and the determination to do the Father's will, and thus conquered life and death.
t071.s5.i2: Even before apparent defeat and the anguish of despair, Jesus stood calm and unafraid in the divine presence.
t071.s5.i3: Jesus encouraged a fear-ridden young man that suffering would give vigor, disappointment a spur, and obstacles a stimulus.
t071.s5.i4: Jesus taught the multitude gathered at Bethsaida for more than an hour on "the mission of adversity and the spiritual value of disappointment."
t071.s5.i5: The two hard years before his marriage were a time of real trial in Jesus' earth life.
t072.sum: Growth is the process in which the actual and the potential combine and values are realized in experience; unlike perfect Havona, it is the hallmark of the evolving grand universe and the Supreme Being. Man's spiritual growth proceeds from an awakening to needs to the discernment of meanings and the discovery of values, and it always takes place unconsciously. Man cannot cause growth, but through devotion to supreme values and living faith he can supply its conditions.
t072.s1.i2: Growth is not mere progress; progress is meaningful, but without growth it is relatively valueless.
t072.s1.i3: Values are never static, and change that does not enlarge meanings and elevate values is potential evil.
t072.s1.i4: The supreme value of human life lies in the growth of values, the progress of meanings, and the realization of their cosmic interrelatedness.
t072.s1.i5: Growth of a part is not the same as maturity of the whole; to traverse the psychic circles, the whole personality must grow harmoniously.
t072.s2.h: The Growing Universe and the Supreme Being
t072.s2.i2: Experiential growth implies a creature-Creator partnership, the association of God and man.
t072.s2.i3: The Supreme Being is first a spirit personality derived from the Trinity and second a God of evolutionary growth.
t072.s2.i4: The growth of the whole is the sum of the growth of all its parts, and its completion is an act of the Almighty Supreme.
t072.s2.i5: Creative growth is endless, but along the way moments of satisfying goal attainment become preludes to new adventure.
t072.s3.h: Stages and Signs of Spiritual Growth
t072.s3.i2: True spiritual development shows itself in a life motivated by love, activated by unselfish ministry, and dominated by wholehearted worship.
t072.s3.i3: Spiritual development depends on maintaining a living connection with true spiritual forces and bearing fruit by sharing what one receives with one's fellows.
t072.s3.i4: Spiritual growth is mutually stimulated by intimate association with other religionists, and love is the soil of that growth.
t072.s3.i5: Loyal persons are growing persons, and children are lastingly impressed by the loyalties of the adults with whom they live.
t072.s4.i2: Growth, whether physical, intellectual, or spiritual, is always unconscious; like love, it must grow.
t072.s4.i3: Habits such as sensitivity to divine values, reflective meditation, worshipful problem solving, and avoidance of selfishness favor growth.
t072.s4.i4: The innate drive toward growth is most surely fostered by an attitude of wholehearted devotion to supreme values.
t072.s5.h: Hindrances to Growth and the Teaching of Jesus
t072.s5.i2: Jesus taught not the building of character but the growth of character, and he likened the kingdom of heaven to a mustard seed.
t072.s5.i3: With a carpenter's analogy Jesus taught that the soul is a living growth, and mind and morals are the soil from which its higher expressions spring.
t072.s5.i4: The true believer should ask whether he is becoming more skillful in showing goodness today than yesterday, this year than last.
t072.s5.i5: The morontia life forever uproots animal vestiges such as procrastination and evasion, so that growth may continue.
t073.sum: Science explores the world of facts and energy-matter by reason, and religion experiences values and spiritual realities by faith. They are independent domains starting from different postulates; philosophy seeks to coordinate them, and revelation affirms that the First Cause of science and the saving God of religion are one and the same. Science purifies religion by clearing away superstition, and religion gives the impulse of brotherhood by which the civilization of a scientific age can live together.
t073.s1.i3: Science assumes without proof the reality of matter, motion, and life; religion assumes mind, spirit, and the Supreme.
t073.s1.i5: In science the idea precedes its expression, but in religion the experience of realization precedes the expression of the idea.
t073.s2.i1: God is to science a cause, to philosophy an idea, and to religion a person, the loving heavenly Father.
t073.s2.i2: The existence of God can never be proved by scientific experiment or pure logic; it is realized only in human experience.
t073.s2.i3: Reason may reach a First Cause by studying nature, but faith is needed to transform it into a God of salvation.
t073.s2.i4: Revelation affirms that the First Cause of science and the saving God of religion are the same Deity.
t073.s2.i5: In science God is a possibility, in philosophy a probability, and in religion a certainty.
t073.s3.i2: Evolutionary religion must be continually refined by the censorship of revelation and in the crucible of true science.
t073.s3.i3: Science enables man to control his physical environment, and religion gives the impulse of brotherhood that lets people live together in the complex civilization of a scientific age.
t073.s3.i4: Both science and religion need more searching and fearless self-criticism, and teachers in both fields are often too dogmatic.
t073.s3.i5: Harmonizing the discoveries of science with the insights of religion requires a sincere desire to follow truth wherever it leads.
t073.s4.i1: Science discovers the material world, religion evaluates it, and philosophy seeks to interpret meanings by coordinating both viewpoints.
t073.s4.i2: Harmonizing science and religion is difficult because of ignorance of the intervening domain of morontia; the morontia viewpoint removes the difference.
t073.s4.i3: Metaphysics is man's earnest but futile attempt to compensate for the absence of the morontia mota.
t073.s4.i4: Revelation does not originate science or religion; its function is to coordinate both with the truth of reality.
t073.s4.i5: True revelation never renders science unnatural, religion unreasonable, or philosophy illogical.
t073.s5.i1: The statements on physical science in revelatory papers will soon need revision, and their cosmology is not inspired.
t073.s5.i3: Scientists unintentionally plunged mankind into a materialistic panic, but the religion of Jesus has never become bankrupt.
t073.s5.i4: What science has destroyed is only childish illusions born of mistaken interpretations; true religion remains untouched.
t074.sum: Philosophy is the effort of the human mind to weave the facts revealed by science and the values experienced by religion into one coherent view of the universe; it is the domain of wisdom. Its body is founded on material facts, while its soul and energy come from spiritual insight. The highest attainable philosophy rests on the reason of science, the faith of religion, and the truth insight of revelation, and the philosophic quest does not end even on Paradise.
t074.s1.i2: The body of philosophic thought must be founded on material facts, but its soul and energy is mortal spiritual insight.
t074.s1.i3: Philosophy arose from the effort to organize the separate findings of science and religion into a reasoned and unified attitude toward the universe.
t074.s1.i4: Science is the domain of knowledge, religion the sphere of the faith experience, and philosophy the realm of wisdom.
t074.s1.i5: Science is satisfied with a First Cause, religion with a supreme personality, and philosophy with unity.
t074.s2.h: The Place and Limits of Philosophy
t074.s2.i1: In science the self observes the material world, philosophy observes this observation, and religion experiences the reality that observes it all.
t074.s2.i3: Philosophy inclined to matter becomes naturalism, overweighted toward spirit becomes mysticism, and leaning on metaphysics ends in skepticism and confusion.
t074.s2.i4: Philosophy should not project reality only by straight-line logic but should allow for the elliptic symmetry of reality and the curvature of relation concepts.
t074.s2.i5: A philosophy useful to both science and religion avoids the extremes of materialism and pantheism and recognizes the reality of personality, the changeless in the midst of change.
t074.s3.i2: Philosophy clarified by revelation can function adequately even in the absence of the morontia mota and despite the failure of metaphysics.
t074.s3.i3: True philosophy grows out of the wisdom that seeks to correlate the quantitative observations of science with the qualitative observations of religion.
t074.s3.i4: The lower planes of the morontia mota join directly with the highest levels of human philosophy.
t074.s3.i5: The ideal human state is one in which wisdom, faith, and experience work together, meaningfully fusing philosophy, religion, and science into one.
t074.s4.h: The Formation of a Philosophy of Religion
t074.s4.i1: An individual's philosophy of religion is formed from many factors, including inner experience, environment, temperament, education, and social conditions.
t074.s4.i3: The philosophy of religion evolves through four levels, from conformity to tradition to fearless and sincere thinking and living.
t074.s4.i4: A sound philosophy of religion distinguishes material and spiritual realities while recognizing their unity in intellectual striving and social service.
t074.s4.i5: An effective philosophy of living weaves together cosmic insight and emotional reactions to the environment.
t074.s5.h: Philosophy in History and the Eternal Quest
t074.s5.i2: The Greek philosophers achieved lofty ethical systems, but their concept of God dissolved in a pantheistic haze and failed to satisfy the masses' longing for salvation.
t074.s5.i3: Religion has long endured without philosophy, but philosophy wholly unconnected with religion has seldom endured long.
t074.s5.i4: Even on Paradise endless mysteries remain for philosophy to solve, and the exhilaration of philosophy is a satisfaction second only to worship.
t074.s5.i5: The masters of philosophy on Paradise delight in leading ascenders in the thrilling quest of solving universe problems.
t075.sum: Revelation is the direct presentation by the real spiritual world of the truth that evolutionary religion seeks by circuitous ways, and it sorts and elevates evolutionary religion. Truth is autorevelation when it comes through the Adjuster and epochal revelation when it comes through celestial beings. Urantia has had five epochal revelations; revelation keeps in touch with evolution so as not to be too far removed from the thought of its age, and it coordinates science, religion, and philosophy as one truth.
t075.s1.i3: Revealed religion is always characterized by belief in a Deity of final values and a concept of the survival of personality after death.
t075.s1.i4: To elevate evolutionary religion, revelation must present teachings not too far removed from the thought of its age.
t075.s1.i5: The morality of evolutionary religion drives by fear, but revealed religion leads people to seek a God of love through the longing to be like him.
t075.s2.i1: There have been only five revelations of epochal significance; the first was the Dalamatia teachings of the one hundred of Caligastia's staff.
t075.s2.i2: The second was the Edenic teachings of Adam and Eve; though interrupted by the default of the Garden, the Sethite priests carried on part of them.
t075.s2.i3: The third was the revelation of Machiventa Melchizedek of Salem, who taught trust and faith.
t075.s2.i4: The fourth was Jesus of Nazareth, who revealed God as the Universal Father and taught love and service.
t075.s2.i5: The fifth is the Urantia Papers, presented jointly by many beings.
t075.s3.i3: That the First Cause of science is a Father full of mercy can be known only through revelation.
t075.s3.i4: Revelation does not originate science or religion; its function is to coordinate both with the truth of reality.
t075.s3.i5: Revelation is validated only by human experience, and it confirms the harmony of the approaches of science, religion, and philosophy.
t075.s4.i1: The revelators give preference to the highest existing human concepts and resort to pure revelation only when there is no adequate expression.
t075.s4.i2: These papers are based on more than a thousand human concepts gathered from God-knowing mortals.
t075.s4.i3: The laws of revelation forbid imparting unearned or premature knowledge, so the cosmology contained in revelation soon becomes outdated.
t075.s4.i4: Revelation is a spiritual phenomenon, but its statements on cosmology are not inspired; their value lies in reducing error and restoring lost knowledge.
t075.s4.i5: Because of the isolation of rebellion, the revelation of truth was mixed with transient cosmologies, but eternal truth should not be slighted for that reason.
t075.s5.i1: Revelation compensates for the absence of the morontia viewpoint, providing a technique of unity for understanding the relationships of matter and spirit.
t075.s5.i3: Revelation compensates for the weaknesses of evolving philosophy and accomplishes what metaphysics could not.
t075.s5.i4: Revelation liberates man for the eternal adventure and gives assurance of the survival of personality.
t075.s5.i5: Revelation glorifies man and discloses his capacity to be a partner with God.
t076.sum: The Lucifer rebellion was the revolt launched some two hundred thousand years ago by Lucifer, sovereign of the system of Satania, together with his first assistant, Satan. It began with a "Declaration of Liberty" that denied the reality of the Father, the sovereignty of Michael, and the ascension plan. Thirty-seven Planetary Princes joined it, and Urantia was among their worlds. The rebellion sprang from self-contemplation and pride; the universe rulers waited long so that every being could make a full choice, and Michael's bestowal virtually ended the rebellion.
t076.s1.h: Lucifer and the Origin of the Rebellion
t076.s1.i1: Lucifer was not an ascendant being but a brilliant Son created in the local universe, and he ruled Satania with its 607 inhabited worlds.
t076.s1.i3: No special conditions in Satania favored rebellion; the idea of revolt originated in Lucifer's own mind.
t076.s1.i4: In a pride that led to self-deception, he at some point became disloyal, and evil turned into deliberate sin.
t076.s1.i5: On Urantia Lucifer entrusted his cause to his first assistant, Satan, and Caligastia took his side here.
t076.s2.i1: Lucifer claimed that the Universal Father did not really exist and was a myth invented by the Sons to maintain their rule.
t076.s2.i2: He demanded self-government for the local systems and attacked the sovereignty of Michael and the interference of the Ancients of Days as tyranny.
t076.s2.i3: He denounced the plan of long training for ascending mortals as a waste of time and energy.
t076.s2.i5: Lucifer pointed to the merciful delays of justice as proof that the government of the Sons was incompetent.
t076.s3.h: War in Heaven and Its Losses
t076.s3.i1: Michael, not yet having completed his bestowals, chose noninterference, and Gabriel led the loyal hosts.
t076.s3.i2: The war in heaven was not a physical conflict, but it was far more deadly because eternal life was at stake.
t076.s3.i3: Thirty-seven Planetary Princes joined the rebellion; only on Panoptia did the people refuse to follow their prince and stand with Michael.
t076.s3.i4: The angelic orders suffered the greatest losses, yet no being of Paradise origin and none of the Trinitized Sons went astray.
t076.s4.i1: The greatest confusion left by the Lucifer rebellion came from the failure to distinguish true liberty from false liberty.
t076.s4.i3: Liberty becomes self-destroying when it is divorced from justice, fairness, forbearance, moral obligation, and spiritual values.
t076.s4.i4: Lucifer's folly lay in attempting to short-circuit time in an experiential universe.
t076.s5.h: The Wisdom of Delay and the End of the Rebellion
t076.s5.i2: It was advised that an arbitrary suppression would have led at least three times as many beings astray.
t076.s5.i3: Michael offered the rebels forgiveness and restoration to service if they repented, but none of the leaders accepted.
t076.s5.i4: Michael's bestowal ended the rebellion throughout Satania, and Lucifer was afterward detained by the Ancients of Days.
t076.s5.i6: The Melchizedeks teach that the good resulting from the Satania rebellion is more than a thousand times the sum of all the evil.
t077.sum: Caligastia was the Planetary Prince who came to Urantia some five hundred thousand years ago, a Lanonandek Son of rich experience and a brilliant career, who joined the Lucifer rebellion and betrayed the world entrusted to him. His apostasy isolated Urantia from the universe circuits, sixty members of the planetary staff followed him, and the culture of Dalamatia collapsed. He later entrapped Adam and Eve, and after Jesus defeated him on Mount Hermon he lost the power to invade the minds of men.
t077.s1.i1: Caligastia was a secondary Lanonandek Son with rich experience in the administration of the local universe and of Satania.
t077.s1.i2: Lucifer promoted him to his personal staff, and he had long sought appointment as a Planetary Prince.
t077.s1.i3: He had a record of loyalty and devotion, but also a restless temperament and a tendency to oppose the established order.
t077.s1.i5: He arrived about five hundred thousand years ago, when the Sangik races were appearing, and set up his headquarters in the Mesopotamian region.
t077.s2.i1: His associate assistant, Daligastia, headed the staff, and one hundred volunteers chosen from Jerusem formed the corporeal staff.
t077.s2.i2: The Life Carriers transplanted the life plasm of one hundred male and female descendants of Andon and Fonta into the material bodies of the staff.
t077.s2.i3: The Dalamatian revelation, the first teaching of the staff, lasted more than three hundred thousand years until it was interrupted by secession.
t077.s3.i1: At Satan's visit in the three hundred thousandth year of his rule, Caligastia agreed to betray the planet once the rebellion was proclaimed.
t077.s3.i3: Daligastia proclaimed Caligastia "God of Urantia," and at that moment the system circuits were cut and Urantia was isolated.
t077.s3.i4: Van declared this tantamount to planetary rebellion and protested, and after a struggle of more than seven years the loyalists were vindicated.
t077.s3.i5: Forty members of the staff refused to rebel; the sixty who rebelled chose Nod as their leader and were reduced to mortal status.
t077.s4.i2: Amadon, of lesser intellect, remained loyal to the end, showing that loyalty counts more than intelligence in spiritual choice.
t077.s4.i3: His plan to rebuild society at once on his ideas of personal and group liberty failed, plunging the world into deeper confusion.
t077.s4.i4: One hundred and sixty-two years after the rebellion, Dalamatia sank beneath the sea.
t077.s4.i5: Afterward twelve Melchizedek receivers administered the planet, and Van established outposts of civilization throughout the world.
t077.s5.h: From the Days of Adam to the Days of Jesus
t077.s5.i1: Caligastia and Daligastia hindered the preparation of the Garden of Eden and confused its inhabitants with teachings of unbridled liberty.
t077.s5.i3: Serapatatia, though well-meaning, never realized that he was playing into the hands of Caligastia and Daligastia.
t077.s5.i4: Jesus met Caligastia alone on Mount Hermon and prevailed, after which Caligastia's apostasy was virtually settled.
t077.s5.i5: Before leaving Urantia, Michael offered mercy to Caligastia and Daligastia, but they rejected his offer.
t078.sum: Adam and Eve were a Material Son and Daughter of Jerusem who came about thirty-eight thousand years ago as biologic uplifters to Urantia, a world isolated by rebellion. They worked in the Garden of Eden for one hundred and seventeen years, but through Eve's impatience to hasten results and Adam's errors of judgment they turned aside from the divine plan and defaulted. They were reduced to mortal status yet cleared of the charge of rebellion, and through the violet race they made a great contribution to the biologic and cultural progress of mankind.
t078.s1.i1: Material Sons and Daughters are the offspring of the Creator Son, destined to serve as physical uplifters on the evolutionary worlds.
t078.s1.i2: After the inspection and recommendation of Tabamantia, Adam and Eve were sent to Urantia, a world retarded and isolated by rebellion.
t078.s1.i3: They were members of the senior corps of Material Sons on Jerusem, an experienced pair who had led research on the modification of life forms.
t078.s1.i4: The entire senior corps volunteered, and Adam and Eve, who had stayed loyal during the Lucifer rebellion, were chosen.
t078.s1.i5: They arrived 37,848 years before A.D. 1934, in the season when the Garden was in full bloom.
t078.s2.h: The Culture of the Garden of Eden
t078.s2.i1: The schools of Eden taught health, the golden rule, individual and group rights, play, and competition, aiming at socialization.
t078.s2.i2: Adam discouraged set prayers and taught that effective prayer must be the personal longing of the soul.
t078.s2.i3: Adam sought to awaken sex equality by teaching that woman contributes equally with man to new life.
t078.s2.i4: Traditions such as the six days of creation and the rib story are later confusions and condensations of events from the Garden days.
t078.s3.i1: They faced deep loneliness in a world of spiritual darkness, wholly unprepared to accept brotherhood.
t078.s3.i3: Caligastia often visited the Garden urging easier ways, but at first they firmly rejected every proposal of compromise.
t078.s3.i4: Serapatatia sincerely wanted to help the world but never knew that he had become Caligastia's tool.
t078.s4.i1: In her secret meeting with Cano, Eve broke the long-standing warning against mixing good and evil.
t078.s4.i3: Realizing the failure, Adam in despair committed the same folly as Eve, and enraged inhabitants destroyed a Nodite settlement.
t078.s4.i4: They left the Garden for the second garden, and their children who had reached twenty could choose the way to Jerusem.
t078.s4.i5: Gabriel adjudged them in default but cleared them of the charge of rebellion against the universe government.
t078.s5.h: There Was No Fall of Man
t078.s5.i2: The Adamic bestowal greatly improved mankind biologically, and Adam should not be regarded as the cause of a curse on the human race.
t078.s5.i3: After their demotion to mortal status they sincerely repented, and Thought Adjusters came to indwell them.
t078.s5.i4: In the second garden Adam left his life plasm, adding 1,570 superior men and women to the world.
t078.s5.i5: Adam lived 530 years and, after death, awoke in a special resurrection and attained citizenship on Jerusem.
t079.sum: Machiventa Melchizedek was a Melchizedek who incarnated as an emergency Son at Salem in Palestine 1,973 years before the birth of Jesus, at a time when the truth of the one God was dying out after Adam's failure. For ninety-four years he taught the covenant that God's favor is received by faith alone in El Elyon, the Most High, and through Abraham he ensured that this truth would be carried on. He prepared the way for Michael's bestowal and is now called the vicegerent Planetary Prince of Urantia.
t079.s1.i1: For thousands of years after the failure of Adam's mission, revealed truth was in danger of extinction, and by about 3000 B.C. the concept of God had grown very dim.
t079.s1.i2: Machiventa volunteered from among the twelve planetary receivers and made an emergency Son incarnation, one of only six in the history of Nebadon.
t079.s1.i4: He appeared in the tent of the herder Amdon, ate material food for the first time, and that night began to reveal the truth of God's reality.
t079.s1.i5: He received a Thought Adjuster but never married and could leave no offspring; his body was of the type of the one hundred staff members.
t079.s2.i1: He founded a school at Salem modeled on the training system of the Sethite priests and was known as "priest of El Elyon" and "the sage of Salem."
t079.s2.i3: The Salem creed was to believe in the Most High, accept the covenant that he grants favor for faith rather than sacrifice, and keep the seven commandments.
t079.s2.i5: He permitted no sacrifices at Salem and offered the sacrament of bread and wine in place of blood offerings.
t079.s2.i6: The three concentric circles symbolized the Paradise Trinity, but most understood them as the three kingdoms of men, angels, and God.
t079.s3.i1: The Melchizedek receivers had long observed Abraham's ancestors, and the family of Terah met their expectations.
t079.s3.i2: Abraham, who harbored ambitions to become king, won the battle of Siddim despite Melchizedek's dissuasion and then paid him tithes.
t079.s3.i4: Melchizedek again brought the news that salvation comes by faith, but the Semitic tribes went back to the system of blood sacrifice.
t079.s3.i5: The covenant was completed after Abraham publicly renounced his personal ambitions, and more than one hundred thousand people were enrolled in the Salem brotherhood.
t079.s4.h: The Purpose and Spread of the Mission
t079.s4.i2: He taught that another Son of God would come, born of a woman.
t079.s4.i3: Salem missionaries went beyond Egypt, Mesopotamia, and Asia Minor, reaching Europe and the British Isles.
t079.s4.i4: Michael appeared on earth and confirmed everything that Melchizedek had taught about the Paradise Father.
t079.s4.i5: Because Melchizedek's teachings had been lost, few recognized Michael when he came in the flesh.
t079.s5.i1: When people began to regard him superstitiously as a demigod, he left suddenly, soon after the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah.
t079.s5.i2: His disappearance left Abraham with a grief he never overcame for the rest of his life.
t079.s5.i3: What the Old Testament describes as conversations between Abraham and God were actually conferences between Abraham and Melchizedek.
t079.s5.i4: For nineteen centuries he worked with the prophets to preserve the truth of Salem, and he is now called the vicegerent Planetary Prince of Urantia.
t080.sum: Mankind on Urantia began nearly a million years ago with Andon and Fonta, and about five hundred thousand years ago the six colored races, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and indigo, appeared all at once in one Sangik family. The violet race of Adam and Eve was later added, forming the Andites, and no pure races remain today. The races differ in mental outlook and capacity, yet all races have the same standing before heaven and are indwelt by the same spirit.
t080.s1.i1: Urantia was registered as an inhabited world when the twins, the first two human beings, were eleven years old.
t080.s1.i3: Mankind has a history of nearly a million years; the Andonites avoided the forests and made progress in open lands and higher latitudes.
t080.s1.i4: Again and again in Urantia's history superior stocks have mixed with inferior stocks and deteriorated.
t080.s2.h: The Emergence of the Six Sangik Races
t080.s2.i1: About five hundred thousand years ago, in the highlands of northwestern India, a Sangik family produced unusually intelligent children.
t080.s2.i3: On an average planet the races appear one after another beginning with the red, but on Urantia the six races came from one family at the same time.
t080.s2.i4: The red, yellow, and blue are primary races and the orange, green, and indigo secondary, and their intellectual and spiritual gifts overlap.
t080.s2.i5: Differentiation into the various colored races gives mankind desirable variation that could not be obtained otherwise.
t080.s3.i1: Driven out of Asia by the yellow man, the red man crossed to North America about eighty-five thousand years ago, where Onamonalonton for a time restored peace.
t080.s3.i2: The yellow race first achieved settled agriculture and social cooperation and, under Singlangton's leadership, worshiped "One Truth."
t080.s3.i3: The orange and green races, after endless strife, were absorbed into other races and disappeared.
t080.s3.i4: The blue man invented the spear and laid the foundations of the modern arts; the so-called white race is mainly descended from him.
t080.s3.i5: The violet race of Adam and Eve spread out from the second garden and blended with the Nodites and Sangik races to become the Andites.
t080.s4.i1: Diversity stimulates natural selection and healthy competition, and differences among races foster tolerance and altruism.
t080.s4.i4: The blending of superior and dissimilar stocks produces new and vigorous strains, and the dangers of race mixture have been much exaggerated.
t080.s4.i5: Most objection to race mixture rests on social and cultural prejudice rather than on biology.
t080.s5.i3: Human unity and brotherhood can be achieved only through the religion of the spirit, which is personal experience, not through religions of authority.
t080.s5.i4: The risen Jesus commanded that the gospel of the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man be wisely carried to all nations and races.
t080.s5.i5: Pentecost wiped out all religious discrimination based on race, culture, caste, or sex.
